Families of lessons: rows of [the catalogue](lessons.md) that share one shape,

## A check that cannot fail

**Rule.** A check counts as protection only once it has been seen to fail on its subject, and its verdict comes from the measured result, never from reaching the end.

**Guard recipe.** Give every check a fixture or mutation built to fail and require red at the assertion; read exit codes, not tails; assert that tests actually ran and name one; finished and succeeded are separate states; a guard cell names only what an automated run invokes.

## A copy of a fact drifts from its source

**Rule.** Every fact has one statement; every other place derives it or is tested against it.

**Guard recipe.** Generate views from the source and fail CI when they are stale; tests read the registry or manifest instead of restating it; adapted copies pin their source commit and are polled for drift.

## A failure nobody is told about in time

**Rule.** Every failure reaches a person who is told, at the earliest gate it could be caught.

**Guard recipe.** Checks fail as workflows that notify, never only a page; the gate runs on every pull request, not only the trunk; settings held by a third party are checked before they are relied on and report into a room someone is in.

## A read trusted after the world moved

**Rule.** A value read, checked or derived at one moment is used only while what it was read from is unchanged and held by the same guard.

**Guard recipe.** Keep the checked bytes through use; take related reads together; key every lock to the state it protects and make every writer honour it; one re-derive path every writer of an input calls; test with two real writers and a slow call held open.

## A rule tested alone

**Rule.** A rule is tested against everything else that applies to the same input: every entrance, axis, copy and enclosing condition, not the one case reported.

**Guard recipe.** State the invariant once and loop it over every entrance, axis or copy; test each condition with its neighbour both ways; test a rule against the rules that take precedence over it; break the fix several ways before believing the test.

## A test that does not own its inputs

**Rule.** A test controls every input its result depends on (the clock, its random draws, the work it starts) and leaves nothing running when it ends.

**Guard recipe.** Inject the clock and rerun the suite with it moved forward; derive assertions from the draw and print it on failure; everything a test starts goes on a list its teardown drains and awaits.

## A wait not sized to what it waits on

**Rule.** Every wait waits on the condition itself, with a deadline measured from what it waits on, on each attempt, and running out is a reported failure.

**Guard recipe.** Replace sleeps and tick counts with a condition wait plus an explicit deadline and message; put the deadline on the attempt, not between attempts; size limits from a measured distribution or the human act; a test asserts that timing out fails loudly.

## A write destroys what it does not own

**Rule.** Before writing, a writer confirms the target is its own and that everything its write removes is something it means to remove.

**Guard recipe.** Check an identity marker or ownership record before the first write, and that a new file's name is free; refuse to overwrite an edited target; round-trip an untouched record byte for byte; append a marker to each generated file, regenerate, and fail if it survives; deliberate breaks run in a separate worktree.

## Lost reads as empty

**Rule.** Absence is never allowed to look like a healthy empty: anything produced, typed or entered either survives or fails loudly.

**Guard recipe.** Missing means missing: skip or fail, never coerce to an empty value; a test injects a new item, a failure or a first-time file and asserts it is still there, visible or reported (git status --porcelain, a remainder view, the failure path restoring input).

## What you test is not what runs

**Rule.** Test the thing a stranger actually gets, through the path it actually takes: the shipped package, the committed tree, the real input, the real boundary.

**Guard recipe.** Build the shipped artifact in the test (npm pack, the exact staged paths) and run from it; inject values through the channel every path reads, including spawned processes; drive real input where a person's matters; fakes model the third party's recorded behaviour; run embedded code through its own parser.
